question.worked_solution:
First, note that $x=0$ cannot be a solution. This is because if $x=0,$ then the rational term would be $\frac{9}{2\cdot 0},$ which is undefined because it has a zero denominator.

To solve the equation, we first multiply both sides by $(2x)$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{2x} & =3 \\ 2x\cdot \frac{9}{2x} & =3\cdot 2x \\ \cancel{2x}\cdot \frac{9}{\cancel{2x}} & =6x \\ 9 & =6x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}9 & =6x \\ \frac{9}{6} & =\frac{6x}{6} \\ \frac{3}{2} & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Since  $x=\frac{3}{2}$ is different from $x=0$, we can accept it as a solution. Thus, the solution is $x=\frac{3}{2}.$
